Support running Kubernetes-in-Kubernetes, as UserNS-enabled pods

Usernetes can now be deployed inside an existing Kubernetes cluster, as
pods running in user namespaces (hostUsers: false, KEP-127), without
privileged: true. This is the Kubernetes-in-Kubernetes analog of
running Usernetes inside Rootless Docker.

The project generation is bumped from Gen2 to Gen3. Gen3 is a superset
of Gen2: the Kubernetes-in-Docker (Docker Compose) mode remains the
default deployment mode.

Changes:
- kubernetes/usernetes.yaml: StatefulSets for the control plane and the
  workers, plus a headless Service for stable DNS names. Instead of
  privileged: true, the node pods get namespaced capabilities, an
  unmasked procfs, and unconfined seccomp/AppArmor profiles, all
  contained by the user namespace. The node pods prefer spreading
  across the nodes of the outer cluster (topologySpreadConstraints).
- kubernetes/Makefile: `make up / kubeadm-init / install-flannel /
  kubeadm-join / kubeconfig / port-forward / ...`, mirroring the
  top-level Makefile. Multiple inner clusters (tenants) can be created
  in the same outer cluster by changing U7S_NAMESPACE.
- Dockerfile: copy the source tree into /usernetes so that the image is
  self-contained (still shadowed by the bind mount in the Compose mode).
- u7s-entrypoint.sh: set net.ipv4.ip_forward and relax rp_filter
  (best-effort), as pod specs cannot set unsafe sysctls.
- CI: smoke-test this mode, including multi-tenancy, with k3s as the
  outer cluster, and with a two-node outer cluster emulated using Lima
  (hack/create-outer-cluster-lima.sh) to cover the inner Flannel VXLAN
  traffic across the outer nodes
  (.github/workflows/reusable-k8s-in-k8s.yaml).
- CI: push the node image to ghcr.io/rootless-containers/usernetes
  (.github/workflows/image.yaml) on pushes to master and on tags; the
  ":master" image is the default U7S_IMAGE of kubernetes/Makefile.

Notable pitfalls solved (see kubernetes/README.md for the details):
- The CRI of the outer cluster has to mount /sys/fs/cgroup of the node
  pods read-write, so that systemd inside them can manage its own
  (namespaced) cgroups; otherwise systemd exits immediately with
  "Failed to create /init.scope control group: Read-only file system".
  For containerd (>= 2.1), this corresponds to `cgroup_writable =
  true`, preferably set on a dedicated runtime handler that is exposed
  to the node pods as a RuntimeClass (U7S_RUNTIME_CLASS_NAME); for
  CRI-O, to the `cgroup2-mount-hierarchy-rw.crio.io` annotation.
- The subnets of the inner cluster must not overlap with the subnets of
  the outer cluster; otherwise the routes installed by the inner
  Flannel shadow the node pods of the outer cluster. So this mode
  defaults to 10.200.0.0/16 and 10.201.0.0/16 (U7S_POD_SUBNET and
  U7S_SERVICE_SUBNET), unlike the Compose mode that keeps 10.244.0.0/16
  and 10.96.0.0/16 (POD_SUBNET and SERVICE_SUBNET in the top-level
  Makefile). The subnets do not need to differ across the tenants.
- The kube-proxy DaemonSet of the inner cluster is patched to drop
  privileged: true in favor of NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW: the sandbox of a
  privileged pod with hostNetwork gets a fresh read-write sysfs mount,
  which cannot be fulfilled inside a userns node pod, as the network
  namespace of the node pod is owned by the initial user namespace, not
  by the user namespace of the pod.
- /boot of the hosts is mounted into the node pods (as in the Compose
  mode), as the kubeadm preflight checks want to read the kernel config.

Tested end-to-end (up to hack/test-smoke.sh) against kubeadm-based
(single-node and two-node) and k3s-based outer clusters (Kubernetes
v1.36, containerd 2.3, runc 1.5, kernel 7.0).

kubernetes: allow creating privileged pods in the inner cluster

For a privileged pod, runc has to mount a fresh read-write sysfs, which
the kernel allows in a mount namespace owned by a user namespace only
when the mount namespace already contains a fully-visible read-write
sysfs instance. The /sys of the node pods is mounted read-only by the
CRI of the outer cluster, and the node pods cannot mount a read-write
instance by themselves, so it has to be provided by the host, at
/run/usernetes/sysfs, and mounted into the node pods via a hostPath
volume. The parent directory is mounted instead of the sysfs itself,
as sysfs does not support the idmapped mounts that the kubelet uses
for the volumes of UserNS-enabled pods.

This issue does not occur in the Docker Compose mode: there the node
container runs with `privileged: true` (which is safe under Rootless
Docker, as it only grants the capabilities that are namespaced in the
RootlessKit user namespace), so Docker mounts its /sys read-write,
which already satisfies the visibility requirement. A UserNS-enabled
Kubernetes pod cannot be privileged, and the CRI has no option for
mounting /sys of an unprivileged pod read-write (unlike
`cgroup_writable` for cgroups).

Privileged pods with hostNetwork can be created even without this fix,
although their /sys is a read-only bind mount of the /sys of the node
pod, as mounting a fresh sysfs requires the network namespace to be
owned by the user namespace. The network namespace of a node pod is
created by the CRI of the outer cluster, i.e., owned by the initial
user namespace; this also cannot happen in the Docker Compose mode,
where the network namespace is created inside the RootlessKit user
namespace.

CI: add Rawhide (Podman 6)

Two issues had to be addressed for the Rawhide CI job:

1. Fedora 46 confines SSH sessions in the new `sshd_session_t` SELinux
   domain, which is not allowed to `name_connect` to most TCP ports.
   `ssh -L PORT:127.0.0.1:PORT` (used for accessing kube-apiserver from
   outside the host) fails with a silent (dontaudit) denial, surfacing as
   "connection reset by peer" on the tunnel client.
   Install a CIL policy module allowing the connection; the `optional`
   block makes it a NOP on distros that do not define `sshd_session_t`.

2. pasta copies the host's IP address into the rootless network namespace
   by default, so connections from inside the node to HOST_IP:PORT
   (e.g., the ClusterIP of the "kubernetes" service resolving to the
   published kube-apiserver port, or kubelet's ExternalIP) terminate at
   the namespace's own tap device instead of hairpinning via the host.
   This crashed kube-flannel ("Failed to create SubnetManager") and left
   CoreDNS in ContainerCreating.
   Configure `pasta_options` with a dedicated address (same as the
   slirp4netns default) so that such connections are routed out to the
   host.

Verified locally on macOS/Lima with
LIMA_TEMPLATE=template://experimental/fedora-rawhide:
create-cluster-lima.sh, test-smoke.sh, and the restart persistency test
all pass.

udev: apply the flannel.1 checksum workaround only for slirp4netns

Analysis of the CI failure of the previous attempt to remove the rule
(both rootless Podman jobs failing with "wget: bad address", while all
Docker and nerdctl jobs passed):

With tx-checksum-ip-generic enabled on flannel.1, the outer UDP
checksum of VXLAN packets is still left unfilled when the packets
reach the tap device of slirp4netns, which is used for Rootless
Podman < 6 (see init-host/init-host.rootless.sh), and slirp4netns
silently drops such packets. Verified with tcpdump on the tap device:
"bad udp cksum" on the outer VXLAN header, packets never reaching the
other host, while non-offloaded UDP packets pass; disabling the
offload on flannel.1 makes DNS work immediately.

Not needed for pasta (Rootless Podman >= 6; Rawhide CI passes without
the rule) or gvisor-tap-vsock (the default network driver of Rootless
Docker >= 29.5, and of nerdctl when slirp4netns is not installed;
`rootlesskit --net=gvisor-tap-vsock` verified in the CI logs).

So apply the rule only when the network is provided by slirp4netns:
Makefile.d/detect-container-engine.sh detects the effective network
driver (`podman info` for Podman; the "rootlesskit" server component
of `docker version`/`nerdctl version` for RootlessKit) and exports
SLIRP4NETNS=1, propagated via docker-compose.yaml to the entrypoint,
which creates /run/u7s-slirp4netns for the udev rule to test (udev
RUN programs cannot see the container's environment variables). The
variable can also be set manually to override the detection.

udev: rename SLIRP4NETNS to FLANNEL_IGNORE_IP_CHECKSUM

The variable controls whether to disable the IP checksum offloading on
flannel.1, and is not inherently specific to slirp4netns (although it is
automatically set to 1 when the container engine provides the network
with slirp4netns). Users who set SLIRP4NETNS=1 manually have to switch
to the new name.

The flag file for propagating the variable to the udev rule is renamed
from /run/u7s-slirp4netns to /run/u7s-flannel-ignore-ip-checksum
accordingly.

Support Calico (VXLAN mode) in addition to Flannel

Usage: `export CNI=calico`, then `make up` and `make install-cni`
(instead of plain `make up` and `make install-flannel`).
Kubernetes-in-Docker mode only; the Kubernetes-in-Kubernetes mode still
supports only Flannel, as calico-node requires `privileged: true` with
hostNetwork, which cannot be fulfilled inside a userns node pod, and
unlike kube-proxy, the DaemonSet cannot be patched to drop the
privileges, as it is reconciled by tigera-operator
(see kubernetes/README.md).

The new `make install-cni` target (available in both modes) installs
$CNI (default: flannel). `make install-flannel` and `make
install-calico` are deprecated in favor of it.

Calico is installed with Helm (like Flannel), from the official
crd.projectcalico.org.v1 and tigera-operator charts pinned in the
Dockerfile. The chart values are rendered from calico-helm-values.yaml
with envsubst, as in kubeadm-config.yaml. The optional components (the
Calico API server, Goldmane, and Whisker) are disabled. Two ports are
published:

- `PORT_CALICO` (default: 4789): the VXLAN port, set via the
  `defaultFelixConfiguration` values of the chart.
- `PORT_CALICO_TYPHA` (default: 5473): the Typha port. Only the host
  port is configurable; the container port is fixed to 5473, as the
  calico-node pods on the other hosts connect to the port number found
  in the endpoints of the calico-typha service.

The Calico-specific hacks below are applied only when the CNI is
explicitly configured to Calico: the CNI environment variable is baked
into the node container by docker-compose.yaml on `make up`, and is
recorded by u7s-entrypoint.sh in /run/u7s-cni. The install-*.sh
scripts and sync-external-ip.sh consult the file, so that an
inconsistent $CNI cannot install the wrong CNI or skip the hacks.
(The scripts cannot read the variable from their own environment:
`podman-compose exec` overrides the environment of the container with
the `environment` of docker-compose.yaml re-interpolated in the
environment of the `podman-compose exec` caller.) The default
(Flannel) configuration is left intact.

Unlike Flannel, Calico needs more than the `public-ip-overwrite`-style
configuration to run in rootless containers:

- sync-external-ip.sh sets the node's InternalIP (in addition to the
  ExternalIP) to HOST_IP, and the Installation values of the chart set
  `nodeAddressAutodetectionV4: kubernetes: NodeInternalIP`, so that
  calico-node picks the routable HOST_IP as the VXLAN tunnel endpoint
  address on every boot (the default autodetection would pick the
  unroutable eth0 address).

- felix refuses to create the vxlan.calico device unless the IPv4
  address of the Calico Node resource (HOST_IP) is assigned to a local
  interface ("unable to find parent interface"). u7s-entrypoint.sh now
  assigns HOST_IP to eth0 as a secondary /32 address.

- felix marks VXLAN packets as NOTRACK, so the conntrack-based NAT of
  the rootless network stack cannot be applied to them.
  u7s-entrypoint.sh sets up stateless NAT (nft `ip saddr set`) instead:
  outbound packets are rewritten from HOST_IP to NODE_IP so that they
  are masqueraded as usual, and inbound packets (whose source address
  is rewritten by the rootless port forwarder) are normalized to the
  sentinel address 169.254.7.115, which is allowed via the
  `externalNodesList` property of the FelixConfiguration, to get
  through felix's "Drop IPv4 VXLAN packets from non-allowed hosts"
  rule.

- The FelixConfiguration also sets `vxlanPort` (PORT_CALICO) and
  `featureDetectOverride: "ChecksumOffloadBroken=true"` (the
  equivalent of Flannel's etc_udev_rules.d_90-flannel.rules).

The smoke test now retries the DNS connectivity check, as the CNI
might still be programming the cross-node routes right after
restarting the nodes.

Verified locally on macOS/Lima (template://ubuntu-24.04 + docker):
cluster bootstrap, test-smoke.sh, and the restart persistency test all
pass with CNI=calico, including a simulation of the environment
override of `podman-compose exec`.
